result.rationale: The diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` in groups_controller#members with no upper bound or validation, then uses it in `members.limit(limit).offset(offset)`. A client can pass an arbitrarily large limit, causing the full member list to be loaded and serialized — a DoS/memory concern introduced by this change (the old code capped implicit behavior differently and only paginated automatic groups). The mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/maximum. That means a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. 1000000), causing the server to fetch and serialize up to that many group members (and effectively the whole group if it has fewer than that).
